doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: George insisted on reading notes; Alvin as his student
summary: He made his players learn the music rather than play by ear, which is why his pupils were good musicians, including Alvin.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: There's so many things we'll think of later that we should have asked you about to your husband. But is there anything else that you can think of now about his way of playing? Did he usually, did he ever do much of the, in the dance band, the faking? Or did he usually use arrangements to have the music written out? That is, did he do it for him in his head?

Well they used to play some pieces by air, you see. Yes. But he believed in his notes. Yeah. He didn't believe in the air music. I think he was making it all. He was making it all. No, he didn't believe in that. The boys couldn't come along with that. Yes, he made them learn the music. He made them learn the music. And that's why everybody that he taught were good musicians. Yes. Because you know Alvin, Alvin's a good musician. Yes, that's right.
Because I can remember him, you know, working on music. I've heard the Alvin talk.

We haven't interviewed Alvin yet. No. For some reason, you know, I mean he's so young and looks so, like you think he didn't know all that old history, but I know that he does. He does. He's always so wonderful.
He's so close to my brother. Yes, my brother. Yeah.

So we'll be getting him some of these days too. But some of those younger fellows, we let them go and we figured we'd get the older people that know more history first, but actually he knows more than most of the young men.
